result.summary:
FAIL (item 3 of the validator list: mutants that survive; items 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7 are closed). F1-F5 of step 16 are really closed (all 12 mutants of steps 16 and 17 killed, each by a test that fails for the right reason), but my own new mutants show three more real gaps of Medium and thirteen of Low, all in the tests only; no defect of the page code that a test must catch was found (one small Low defect of the code is in issues). Verdict FAIL is derived from my own runs; the task named no expected verdict (AP-018).
1. F1-F5 CLOSED. Given mutants (own runs, one at a time, on a copy outside the project, the three page files each time, concurrency 1): N3 -> QP-2d (expected 'b', actual 'd'); N37 -> QP-2d (expected 'b', actual 'a') and QP-9f (a TypeError on a null stored value, a setup effect, QP-2d is the right-reason kill); N35 -> QP-2d (expected 8 writes, actual 7); N4 -> QP-2e (expected nothing chosen, actual 'y'); N5, N5c -> QP-4b; N5b, N5d -> QP-9f (all four fail with a TypeError because the notice node is missing, which is the effect of the mutant; right reason, but the message is not an assertion message); G2 -> QP-9h (expected 'en', actual 'kk'); M24 -> QM-2e only; M29a, M29b -> QM-2d and QP-2g (QP-2g: the page moves to the next question instead of staying). Applied 12, killed 12, survived 0. The table of section 20 (M24, M29) and section 17.5 now match my runs.
N35 NOTE (rule E1 pinned only by the write log): judged a sufficient oracle, not a gap of Medium. The oracle is independent of the code (the count of setItem calls of the test storage), it fails exactly on the mutant, and the property is invisible in the stored value with one tab. It is implementation-bound, though: a value oracle also kills N35 and is stronger. I checked on a copy: after the result screen, overwrite the stored place with another one (as a second tab could), press 'Back', expect the stored place to be the last question again; passes on the real code, fails on N35 (expected 'b', actual 'a'). Optional hardening, Low.
2. NEW MUTANTS (not used in steps 16 and 17): 136 applied, 105 killed, 31 survived. Survivors: 15 equivalent or defensive (V10, V19, V24, W05, W30, W31, X04, X07, X14, Y02, Y09, Y12, Y18, Y19, Z12), 16 real gaps (3 Medium: V04, X05, X06; 13 Low: V05, V11, V28, V31, W07, X03, X13, Y14, Y20, Z01, Z02, T12a, D18_19). No run hung beyond the limit of 150 s; one run is a finding (F3 below).
Survivors explained. Equivalent or defensive: V10 (a null saved version treated as changed: nothing to lose, same screen), V19 (notice reset in 'Start over' is unreachable, a notice card has no such button), V24 (second check of the screen in changeLanguage, no await between it and the first), W05 (AbortError is never produced, the page aborts only by timeout), W30 and W31 (implied by questions_max equals the length and questions_min equals the plain count), X04 (guard in send() is redundant with the guard in advance()), X07 (the shut fieldset gives the field no event), X14 (state.net of kind result is never read), Y02, Y09, Y12 (a browser gives value '' for a bad number and never a blank text; a draft of empty text renders the same), Y18 and Y19 (two guards against a leaked draft, each covers the other; removing both is D18_19), Z12 (a copy of a fresh parsed list).

findings.place: tools/test/picker-page.test.js:287 (QP-1c) and :999 (QP-4a); code tools/src/picker/public/app.js:116-123 (hasSaved, the clause 'the place is not the first question') and :190-194 (the 'k > 0' condition)
findings.what: Design 5.1 (D5) says hasSaved = answers present OR (place is not null and not the first question). The negative side is tested (QP-1c: a stored value with only the language or the first question gives 'Take the survey') but the clause 'place beyond the first question with no answers' is pinned by no test: mutant V04 (the clause removed, hasSaved checks only the answers) passes all 99 tests. This is the same class as F1 of step 16 (a single clause of a two-clause rule). Probe (copy only): the first question is optional, press 'Next' with no answer, reload: the card must offer 'Continue' and it must open question 2; passes on the real code, fails on V04 (Continue missing). Related (Low): V05 ('k > 0' changed to 'k >= 0' when the stored place is taken) passes all tests: a stored place that is not a visible question and no answers must not offer 'Continue'; probe passes on the real code and fails on V05.
findings.fix: TEST-DESIGNER: in QP-1c or QP-4a add (a) the optional-first site: 'Next' with no answer, reload, 'Continue' offered and opens question 2, 'Take the survey' absent; (b) a stored value with the right version, answers {} and current 'zzz' (not a question) or a hidden question: 'Take the survey', no 'Continue'. Mutants V04 and V05 must die.

findings.place: tools/test/picker-page.test.js:1836 (QP-7g); code tools/src/picker/public/app.js:362 (onBack) and :375 (advance, used by 'Skip')
findings.what: QP-7g presses 'Show the result' again, sends the form and Enter during the request, but never 'Skip' or 'Back'; those two buttons stand outside the shut fieldset and stay live while the request is open. Mutant X05 (the guard 'if (state.sending) return' removed from advance) passes all tests: 'Skip' pressed during the request clears the answer and writes the storage while the request already carries that answer, so the stored answers and the result disagree (the second guard in send() comes too late for 'Skip'). Mutant X06 (the guard removed from onBack) passes all tests: 'Back' during the request moves the screen to the previous question while the request is on its way and the result then opens over it. Probes (copy only): on the last optional question with an answer, hold the POST, press 'Skip' and then 'Back': storage snapshot unchanged, same question, still one request; both pass on the real code and fail on the mutants (X06: expected 'Last', actual 'First').
findings.fix: TEST-DESIGNER: in QP-7g, with the POST held, tap 'skip' (on an optional last question with an answer) and 'back', and assert the storage snapshot, the stored answers, the question on the screen and the request count are unchanged; after the answer comes the result opens. Mutants X05 and X06 must die.

findings.what: AP-116 class: assert.equal(page.part("notice"), null, ...) compares a node of the document model with null. When it fails, the message tries to print the node and the run does not finish: with mutant V12 (newVersion shows the notice always) QP-9k alone ran 32 s, took about 6.7 GB of resident memory (measured with /usr/bin/time -l) and was killed by SIGKILL with no test name; in the full file the run stopped after QP-9j at 26 s with 93 of 99 tests reported (QP-9k, QP-9l, QP-11a..11d silently missing), only the exit code 1 and one other failed test told of it. On a 16 GB computer this is a risk, and the failure is not diagnosable. Replacing the second argument by a boolean (page.part("notice") === null, true) makes the same mutant fail in 0.2 s with the test name (checked on a copy).
findings.fix: TEST-DESIGNER: at the two places compare a boolean or the count (page.all('[data-part="notice"]').length, 0) instead of a node with null; look for the same pattern (assert.equal / deepEqual with a node as an argument) in picker-page-model.test.js and the helpers. The failure of QP-9k under V12 must then be reported by name in under a second.
